name: Zerodha
tagline: Bootstrapped discount broker that built India's retail trading habit, profitably
facts: Private, bootstrapped, founder-owned; no IPO plans
14.7% of NSE active clients; steadily declining

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Break every barrier traders and investors face in India: cost, support and technology.

strategy.label: Values
strategy.text: No ads, no spam, no dark patterns; discourage overtrading; build for decades; customer trust over short-term growth.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Flat-fee broking plus best-in-class tools (Kite, Console, Coin); grow by word of mouth and Varsity education.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Trust and pro-trader loyalty, lean team, 45%+ net margins, ecosystem via Rainmatter and Kite APIs.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Diversify beyond F&O: Zerodha Fund House, MTF, merchant banking for new-age IPOs, US investing on Kite.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Is no-marketing still a moat when Groww wins new investors 2x faster? Should Zerodha advertise, list, or stay put?

customers.who: Intraday and F&O traders, mostly metro
customers.pain: Need reliable, fast platform with low costs and pro tools
customers.why: Kite stability, charts, APIs, flat ₹20 pricing and long track record

customers.pain: Hidden fees, mis-selling and spammy upsells at bank brokers
customers.why: Free equity delivery, direct mutual funds via Coin, honest no-push brand

customers.pain: Few brokers offer stable, documented trading APIs
customers.why: Kite Connect APIs and partner ecosystem (Streak, Sensibull, smallcase)

customers.pain: Need distribution and broker integration to reach investors
customers.why: Access to Zerodha's base via Kite integrations and Rainmatter capital

customers.pain: High expense ratios and complex active fund choices
customers.why: Zerodha Fund House: simple, low-cost passive index funds and ETFs

portfolio.key_metrics: AUC, SIP count, Fund House AUM, investor-only share
portfolio.guardrails: Churn to rivals, fund tracking error, fee creep

portfolio.guardrails: Complaint ratio, data breaches, regulatory actions

rows.how: Flat ₹20 or 0.03% per order; equity delivery free; ₹2,738 cr FY26
Interest on MTF book and margins/float; ~₹2,269 cr FY26
Annual demat charge; ~₹180 cr, about 2% of revenue
Expense ratio on AUM; interest on loans against securities

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: Brokerage and interest dominate; F&O-linked income still the profit engine despite SEBI curbs and lost exchange rebates (₹400 cr).

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Long-term investors pay little; a small cohort of active F&O traders generates most brokerage.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: Near-zero CAC (no ads, ~30% referrals historically); ~48% net margin; lean team keeps cost per client tiny.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: MTF, Fund House scale, merchant banking, US investing, wealth for affluent; win back share from Groww.

bullets.label: Headwinds
bullets.text: SEBI F&O rules from Nov 2024 cut F&O activity 20-30%; FY26 lost ~10 lakh active clients.

friction: Kite feels intimidating for first-time investors versus Groww
Separate apps (Kite, Coin, Console) fragment the journey
Support is ticket-based and slow for urgent issues
Account opening and re-KYC still clunky for some
Few hand-holding or advisory features for beginners

competitors.label: Discount brokers

competitors.label: Bank brokers
competitors.text: ICICI Direct, HDFC Sky, Kotak Neo

competitors.label: Wealth / MF
competitors.text: Groww, PhonePe Wealth, INDmoney, Paytm Money

competitors.label: Edge
competitors.text: Trust, pro-grade tech, highest profit margins, no outside investors to please

competitors.label: Risk
competitors.text: Share loss to Groww, F&O dependence, key-person risk, slow diversification
